title: Moon base: the 354-hour night
note: Every sentence comes from the goal's facts in the app (bottlenecks b3.1 and b3.3, the pending promise 'NASA astronauts would visit the Moon's south pole by 2030'). Qualifiers are kept: would, about, mostly, most of the time, in some seasons, has said, yet. The first line says 'would' because the habitat in the picture does not exist.

shots.job: This shot shows a lit habitat through 20 hours of a real dark spell, the stars sliding behind it, so the viewer understands how long a night is for anything that must stay on.
This shot shows a person outside the lit habitat in the dark, so the viewer understands what cannot be switched off.
This shot shows one real month of sunlight sweeping the south pole's ridges, so the viewer understands why the pole is where a base could find power.

This shot shows the same habitat small in the dark landscape through 38 hours of that spell, so the viewer understands that even this ridge goes dark for days and that nothing with a crew has been through it.
This shot shows a person on the same ridge in the low Sun of the sunny season, so the viewer understands what has been promised for 2030.

lines.say: A Moon base would face nights about three hundred and fifty-four hours long.
text: A Moon base would face nights

lines.say: Small landers have survived them by mostly shutting down.
Some ridges at the south pole get sunlight most of the time.
